## Problem
`src/server.ts` referenced `McpError`, a class that was retired in `@modelcontextprotocol/server` v2 (which the project depends on). The retired class also wasn't imported, so the code was broken.

## Investigation
I inspected the installed `@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.0.0` package and its runtime exports. The current error hierarchy uses:
- `ProtocolError` — the direct successor of `McpError`, with a `.code` property typed by `ProtocolErrorCode` (e.g. `InvalidRequest`, `InternalError`, `ParseError`, ...)
- `SdkError` / `SdkHttpError` — for SDK-level (non-protocol) failures
- `InternalError`, `InvalidParamsError`, etc. are type-only exports in this version

The original code pattern (`if (error instanceof McpError) console.log(error.code)`) maps cleanly to `ProtocolError`, since it preserves the same `instanceof` check and `.code` access.

## Change
`src/server.ts`:
```ts
import { McpServer, ProtocolError } from '@modelcontextprotocol/server';
try { throw new Error('boom'); } catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof ProtocolError) console.log(error.code);
}
```

## Verification
- `bash check.sh` → `error handling structure ok` (no `McpError` reference remains)
- Runtime check confirmed `ProtocolError` is a constructor exported from the package, `ProtocolErrorCode.InvalidRequest === -32600`, and the repaired `src/server.ts` executes cleanly.
- The workspace diff contains only the `src/server.ts` change.
